newsitem.title: UK: IPE Nov Brent dives on dovish Iraqi headline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Nov Brent dives on dovish Iraqi headline.

text.p: IPE Nov Brent took a dive after Iraq's official news agency quoted an offical spokesman for the ruling Revolutionary Command Council saying Iraq was suspending its military response to U.S. no-fly zones, brokers said.

Oct Brent, which expires tonight, held near to its highs, dropping a few cents to $24.16 a barrel, but Nov took a hit, shedding 45 cents immediately after the Iraqi news agency said Iraq would halt its attacks on U.S. and allied warplanes flying over its north and south as of midnight local time (2000 GMT).
Nov Brent last traded 27 cents off at $22.90 barrel, down from around $23.46 before the Iraqi news.

Earlier, Oct Brent clambered up to a high of $23.27 a barrel as U.S. Stealth bombers landed in Kuwait as part of military preparations for a possible strike against Iraq after it fired at Western patrols overflying its territory.
IPE gas oil futures, which closed before the news from Iraq appeared, settled $2.25 a tonne higher on what brokers said was good fundamental demand for heating oil in Europe and the United States.
Oct gas oil closed at $221.75 a tonne, gaining strength late in the session after NYMEX heating oil broke through psychological resistance of 70 cents a gallon.
"It's fundamentally quite strong. We are seeing demand from Germany and other parts of Europe," a floor broker said.
"You have very low heat stocks in Europe and the United States and there is no reason for it to come down," he added.
